card: This pull request removes the runtime error state (M_ERROR) from ValidationState and routes fatal runtime and I/O failures through util::Expected<T, kernel::FatalError> instead. BlockValidationState previously conflated block validation failures with runtime system errors, forcing non-validating routines like FlushStateToDisk and InvalidateBlock to take validation state parameters to report disk failures. In addition to clarifying error reporting and updating the libbitcoinkernel API, this unblocks PR 35570 from returning BlockValidationState directly from validation methods.
changed_since_previous: Rebased without fundamental architectural changes; maintains the introduction of `kernel::FatalError` and `util::Expected` across validation and block manager interfaces.
evidence: PR description notes discussions in #33856 and #35570 calling to separate `M_ERROR` from `ValidationState`.
PR description notes this refactoring paves the way for #35570 to return `BlockValidationState` cleanly from validation methods instead of boolean flags.
problem: `BlockValidationState` conflates block validity with unexpected system failures like disk write or memory errors. This forces non-validating functions such as `FlushStateToDisk`, `DisconnectTip`, and `InvalidateBlock` to take a `BlockValidationState` out-parameter solely for error signaling, while validating routines force callers to disentangle three separate outcomes (valid, invalid, or fatal error) from one object.

risk.why: A mistake in propagating fatal error returns across the block connection and activation pipeline could improperly classify hardware or I/O failures as consensus invalidity, or vice versa, causing unexpected node behavior or crashes.

scope_notes: A wide-reaching validation and kernel refactor touching 40 files, replacing `BlockValidationState` out-parameters across chainstate functions with `util::Expected<T, kernel::FatalError>` returns and modifying the libbitcoinkernel C API.
summary: Removes the `M_ERROR` runtime error state from `ValidationState` and decouples system runtime failures from consensus or policy validity. Functions across validation and block storage (including `ConnectBlock`, `AcceptBlock`, `FlushStateToDisk`, `ActivateBestChain`, and `ProcessNewBlock`) are refactored to return `util::Expected<T, kernel::FatalError>`. Corresponding internal error enumerations are also removed from the libbitcoinkernel C API and C++ wrapper.
